REV-1 [R5] R5 requires a tab list with tabs and a tab panel exposed to assistive technology, and the design said SidebarTabs adds the role=tabpanel wiring the library lacks. The panel role is present but the association is not, so a screen reader cannot tell which panel a selected tab controls. Give each tab a stable id plus aria-controls pointing at its panel, and give each panel aria-labelledby pointing back at its tab (the adapter already mutates the library DOM for the tablist name, so the same effect can add these).

REV-2 [USR-004] An existing, already-shipped sidebar behaviour regressed: collapse the pane and expand it again and every app is open again instead of keeping the user's folded state. USR-004 requires the existing behaviour to be frozen before adding the tabs rather than broken. Lift the fold map back into Sidebar and pass it (plus its toggle) into SidebarProjects, or keep SidebarProjects mounted across the rail branch.

REV-3 [R5] The component contract allows a Files tab with no Files panel. The real App always passes an ExplorerPanel, so this is not reachable today, but if explorer is ever absent the selected Files tab has no panel (R5) and no content (R1). Either hide the Files tab when there is nothing to show or render a named panel/hint.

QA-1 [R2] R2's 'stays fixed at the top of the expanded sidebar' and acceptance 'The tab strip keeps the same position with one app as with many' have no test that would fail if the strip were moved below the Projects list. Add an order assertion (topRow/tablist comes before the Projects tabpanel in the expanded nav) and assert the tablist's position is unchanged with many apps.

QA-2 [R2] The edge cases 'tab strip remains visible while the Projects list is scrolled to its bottom' and 'stays inside the sidebar width when the app list is long and names are long' have no test with a scroll or with long names. A 500-row fixture with very long app names would close both.

QA-3 [R1] R1's acceptance 'Files shows the file explorer ... filling the sidebar's available height' has no test that would notice the fill being removed; assert the flex declaration (or a computed layout) on .filesPanel.

QA-4 [R1] The R1 edge case 'The Files tab shows the explorer's existing loading, empty-folder, error and no-folder-hint states unchanged' is only partly covered. Add one case per state rendering the real ExplorerPanel in the Files tab, including root===null with apps present (home folder unknown), which is reachable in the app and is the hint state.

QA-5 [R4] The R4 edge case 'A file operation that closes or re-points an editor tab does not switch the sidebar tab' proves only the close half. Add the aria-selected Files assertion to the rename flow.

QA-6 [R4] R4's acceptance 'With Files active, a new file tab opening in the editor leaves the sidebar on Files' is proven only at Sidebar-stub level, not through the real editor open path. Assert aria-selected Files immediately after the open at App.explorer.test.tsx:726.

QA-7 [R4] The lazy Files mount made these App.explorer assertions race the async listing: the R4 delete/re-point proofs (which live in this file) are flaky under load. Wait for the row (findByTitle or waitFor) after showFiles and after an editor/view change.

QA-8 [R5] The accessibility check 'With focus in the sidebar, Tab reaches the tab strip' is unproven behaviourally; a userEvent.tab() walk from the first sidebar control to the tablist would cover it.

QA-9 [R5] The edge case 'Both tab labels stay legible and clickable when the sidebar is at its narrowest, without horizontal scrolling' has no behavioural proof, and the asserted overflow-x:auto is the opposite of the requirement. Render the strip in a 240px-wide container and assert both labels are fully visible and clickable with no horizontal overflow.

QA-10 [USR-003] The performance acceptance 'a tab switch completes within 100 ms ... and scrolling the Projects list shows no visible freeze' is only indirectly represented by the no-re-render test. The O(1) switch is well evidenced; state the measured budget or how it was checked, and note that the scroll-freeze half is unverified.
